messages.text: Create projects/repo.md — the master plan for projects/repo.html — following the house planning-doc standard. Requisite sections, in order: (0) TURN/STAGE LEDGER: a table of turns/stages with status, where every future build session appends a row before touching code; (1) RELEASES: numbered release list with one-line goals; (2) per-release sections: scope (in/out), build gates (how we verify, on real devices), and backlog of deferred items; (3) FUTURE IDEAS: unscheduled parking lot; (4) IMMUTABLE WORKING RULES: mobile-first, all diagnostics in-app (never DevTools), update-plan-before-code, read-back verification after every push, no stubs or fake data; (5) DECISION LOG: dated owner decisions; (6) APPENDIX: authority order (this plan is the sole authority; chat history loses to the plan). Seed it with what is known so far about projects/repo.html and mark everything else TBD. Keep it tight and scannable on a phone.

messages.text: I want an app that looks at all the repos for acmeproducts that is a dashboard this is the main screen to see what the state of each repo is when it was last accesed, if it is set up for a gitpages - if it is not, there needs to be an option to analyze that repo and determine how to establish a functional launch page if it doesnt exist and to make the necessary config changes, there should be an assessment of what the repo does in some cases there is a one to one releaitnoship between app and repo, when a repo has many apps there needs to be a chevron that opens up that shows the status and a launch link for each app howwever multiple versions must be grouped under a chevron to allow launch of previous versions of the same application in the same repo. the left rail for repo and then a tabbed interface on the right side so there is a repo overview then a repo app tab and whatever is appropriate for that repo maybe its code with code links maybe its readme or install I will leave the details to you but this framework needs to be used so that the right side is custromized for that repo not a onesize fits all approach. Basically I want to get a handle on on my repos and have a central opeerations and control point
